title: Your first network
brief: Build two LANs and join them with a router: PC-A and Switch-1 on 192.168.1.0/24, PC-B and Switch-2 on 192.168.2.0/24. The devices come as out of their boxes: PCs without an address, router ports disabled. Then make PC-A reach PC-B.
steps: Add two PCs, two switches and a router from the build bar, and name them PC-A, PC-B, Switch-1, Switch-2 and Router in the inspector. In Packet Tracer you would drag them from the device list.
Cable PC-A to Switch-1, Switch-1 to the router, the router to Switch-2 and Switch-2 to PC-B: drag from the + of a card to another card. In Packet Tracer: copper straight-through cables.
Give PC-A 192.168.1.10 with prefix length 24, and PC-B 192.168.2.10/24. In Packet Tracer: Desktop, IP Configuration, with the mask 255.255.255.0, which is /24.

Select the router: give port 1, towards Switch-1, 192.168.1.1/24 and port 2, towards Switch-2, 192.168.2.1/24, then turn both ports on. In Packet Tracer: interface g0/0, ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown.
Ping 192.168.2.10 from PC-A, then press Check: the reach goal says why the ping fails.
Give PC-A the default gateway 192.168.1.1 and PC-B 192.168.2.1: the router's address on each LAN. In Packet Tracer: the Default Gateway field.
hints: A cable goes from a card's + to another card, onto the first free port of each.
The router's ports are numbered from 1 in the inspector, in the order the cables were plugged.
A PC sends a datagram for another subnet to its default gateway. Without one, it has nowhere to send it.
